findings.text: the reclaim's MERGE (tomb)-[:REFINED_FROM]->(old) closes a directed cycle in the closing_lineage case, because that case is defined at edit.py:3264-3269 as the target already descending from the tombstone (the successor walk returns the target as the tombstone's live tip), so adding tomb->target on top of the target->...->tomb chain yields tomb->target->...->tomb. The repository treats such a cycle as invalid: graph_store/graph_supersession.py:355 excludes a target the name already descends from and :569 refuses with "REFINED_FROM cycle", edit.py:2325 raises the same refusal for a fold, and chain_history.py:35 walks REFINED_FROM*1.. unbounded, so it would report the revived name as its own ancestor. The node's own test codifies the cycle rather than catching it: tests/standard_names/test_reclaim_superseded_spelling.py:172 asserts TOMBSTONE in retired["successors"], which is exactly the cycle-closing edge.

the fragment asserts zero added failures, but the run's own recorded arms do not support it: baseline_suite names six failing ids and after_suite names eight, and two head ids (tests/standard_names/test_review_pipeline.py::test_audit_embedding_preflight, tests/standard_names/test_review_name_stages.py::TestWorkerUsesCanonicalModel::test_worker_uses_canonical_model) have no counterpart in the recorded base log; the second base run the manifest's baseline_suite note cites as covering them is not on disk, so derived from the two recorded arms the added-failure count is 2. The serial triage at head (logs/triage-head.log, 6 passed, EXIT=0) makes a regression unlikely, but the record's zero rests on an unrecorded arm.

the fragment attributes the recorded 3-passed gate to head f2d466185, but logs/gate-reclaim.log carries no revision or tree header (its first line is a bare '# command:'), and its mtime follows the fix commit ddb434957 which added the receipt assertions the negative control exercises, so the gate log cannot be tied to the revision this review read.

the different_locus case compares the tombstone's locus with the current holder's locus only, and never compares the renaming name's own locus, so a live name from any third locus may take the tombstoned spelling whenever its holder differs; the ruling's stated purpose (the spelling still means what the tombstone recorded) is preserved only if the target also sits at the tombstone's locus, which no test covers.
